title: Loft Dynamics launches Airbus H145 multi-pilot VR simulator, Babcock commits
summary: Babcock France, the country’s largest helicopter emergency medical services operator, is one of the first operators to commit to the newly released platform.
body_text: Loft Dynamics has announced the release of what it said is the world’s first Airbus H145 Multi-Pilot VR Simulator. Now commercially available to operators and training organizations worldwide, the simulator allows H145 pilots and crews to train together in VR for the first time, expanding access to advanced multi-crew training on one of the world’s most widely used helicopter platforms. Babcock France, the country’s largest helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) operator, is one of the first operators to commit to the newly released platform. The company signed a letter of intent at the Farnborough International Airshow for the planned deployment of France’s first H145 VR simulator, which would give H145 -qualified Babcock pilots greater access to frequent, mission-focused training. “The aviation industry faces a growing mismatch: demand for highly trained crews is rising, but access to advanced helicopter simulation remains limited,” said Sebastien Borel, CEO of Loft Dynamics. “The H145 supports a large global community flying some of aviation’s most demanding missions, yet operators have never had a way to train entire crews together in virtual reality. Our H145 Multi-Pilot VR Simulator changes that by making realistic, aircraft-specific multi-crew training accessible enough to become a regular part of how pilots and crews build proficiency. Babcock France’s early commitment carries real weight. It shows that immersive VR is moving beyond an emerging training option and becoming infrastructure that major operators can build into their long-term H145 training strategies.” “The H145 multi-pilot VR simulator is a game-changer for operational safety,” said Romain Trapp, executive vice president, Customer Support and Services, at Airbus Helicopters. “By bringing advanced, accessible training directly to the doorstep of major operators like Babcock, it allows crews to train together frequently and with total precision. We are thrilled to see our partners adopting this immersive technology to enhance crew coordination where it matters most.” Developed in close collaboration with Airbus Helicopters, the simulator enables pilots and crew members to train together in a shared virtual environment for normal, abnormal and emergency procedures. It is built using flight dynamics, systems data and helicopter software provided directly by Airbus Helicopters, and was rigorously tested and validated throughout development by Airbus pilots. The simulator replicates the aircraft’s aerodynamics and performance characteristics, allowing operators to train using the same procedures they follow during flight operations. The system combines a six-degrees-of-freedom full-motion platform, a virtual, full-scale cockpit replica and a 360-degree panoramic field of view to create a highly realistic training experience. It also supports repeated training on complex scenarios that would be difficult, costly or impractical to conduct in an aircraft, including license-related training such as initial type ratings, multi-crew cooperation and instrument training, as well as recurrent training and checking for H145 operators. Babcock France plans to use the simulator across its H145 training program, with a strong focus on mission rehearsal and specialized HEMS and search-and-rescue operations. The company also intends to make simulator capacity available to operators and pilots across France and neighboring countries, helping address the growing shortage of H145 simulator access in the region. “Our mission is to ensure our crews are fully prepared for the complex and critical operations they perform every day,” said Pierre Basquin, chief executive, Aviation, and CEO of Babcock France. “Loft Dynamics’ H145 Multi-Pilot VR Simulator will significantly enhance our training capabilities by enabling more frequent, realistic and collaborative training for pilots and technical crew members. It will strengthen operational readiness, support the highest standards of safety and performance, and expand access to advanced H145 training for operators across France and the region.” Babcock France operates Airbus H145 helicopters and has more than 60 pilots qualified on the type. From 21 HEMS bases across France, its ambulance-configured helicopter fleet provides essential air medical support to hospitals and emergency response networks, completing more than 11,000 missions annually and ensuring patients receive critical care as quickly as possible. This press release was prepared and distributed by Loft Dynamics.

title: Cold Calling vs Cold Emailing: The Ultimate Showdown for 2026
summary: Not sure whether to cold call or cold email? Learn which channel delivers better response rates, conversions, and ROI for modern B2B sales teams.
body_text: Cold calling vs cold emailing: which one wins? Both of them have a very convoluted relationship, where the pros and cons of each approach outweigh one another. I’d say either one of the strategies can be a breadwinner, as long as you have covered all the bases right. How so? If you were to ask a high revenue + high profit company that relies mostly on cold emailing, they are more than likely to favor the email approach over cold calling. Similarly, if you were to pitch the same question to another company that depends on cold calling for better results, while keeping in mind that cold emailing is also part of their sales stack, they are more than likely to respond in favor of their call based campaigns. That ONLY means that in isolated cases, both companies have their KPIs, sub-level strategies, and targets set for emails or cold calls. In fact, both of those can work side by side and bring in even better results, alongside oodles of revenue, of course. We are here to fill you in on both sides of the coin, leaving the decision making process to you. At this point, we also feel obligated to tell you that we’ve been part of the sales calling and emailing circle for a couple of years now. Trellus itself operates as a SaaS cold calling software company with tons of worldwide clients. These clients are either solopreneurs or business owners who have reportedly managed outbound campaigns, booked 100s of meetings and closed over with a very high success/ conversion rate. Their results DID not, in fact, come from choosing one side of the debate. As we mentioned earlier, the best output came from a very smart combination of cold calling, cold emailing, LinkedIn outreach, follow ups, and careful personalization into one repeatable system. That experience also exposed another important lesson. Most people who say cold calling no longer works usually make poor calls. They dial unqualified prospects, read robotic scripts, and give up after hearing a few objections. The same thing happens with email. Sales representatives purchase outdated lists, send generic templates to thousands of contacts, ignore deliverability best practices, and then conclude that cold email has stopped working. Neither channel is broken; Poor execution is. Period… We doubled down on both strategies and wanted to share these key learning points with you: Key Learning Points: The complete difference between cold calling and cold emailing The strengths and weaknesses of both approaches Cold calling vs cold emailing: which has a higher response rate? When should you cold call vs cold email a prospect? Is cold calling or cold emailing more effective for B2B sales? How successful teams combine both into one predictable sales cadence and follow up sequence Best practices and performance benchmarks for 2026 What Is Cold Emailing? A cold email is simply a message sent to someone who has never interacted with your company before. That person has not filled out a contact form, booked a demo, or requested information. You are reaching out because your research suggests there is a genuine business fit. That sounds simple enough, but successful cold emails are built very differently from promotional marketing emails. Marketing emails are designed for subscribers who already know your company. Cold emails begin with zero trust. The recipient has no reason to care about your business, which means every sentence has to earn attention quickly. On the contrary, what usually happens with beginner level solopreneurs and marketers is that they sign up for a cold email outreach software. So far so good! These programs aren’t inherently good or bad. Their effectiveness depends on the features. But coming to the point, these software, or SaaS platforms, have built in cold email templates that you can supposedly customize. Most of the programs automatically pick up on the first and last name of the leads from your lead list, while the subject and the rest of the email body generally cover the purpose of your email. Don’t send those emails as is! Customize them because personalization is not only NOT optional, but it will get you better open and conversion rates. A well written cold email usually answers four simple questions. Who are you? Why are you reaching out specifically to this person? What business problem can you help solve? What action would you like them to take next? Those four questions sound basic, yet many outbound campaigns fail because they never answer them clearly. For example, compare these two opening messages. Poor approach Hi, I'm reaching out because we help companies improve operational efficiencies with our innovative platform. There is nothing memorable here. The message could have been sent to ten thousand companies without changing a single word. Now compare that with this. I noticed your SDR team has doubled in size over the past six months. Companies at that stage often struggle with reply rates because new representatives follow different outreach processes. I thought I'd reach out because we've helped several SaaS teams solve that exact problem. The second version immediately feels more relevant because it speaks directly to something happening inside the prospect's business. This explains why cold email continues to play a central role in modern outbound sales prospecting , especially when combined with phone calls and LinkedIn outreach. Cold Calling vs Cold Emailing Statistics for 2026 Numbers tell a much more balanced story than opinions. Every year, someone claims cold calling has disappeared. Someone else argues email has become too crowded to produce results anymore. Yet companies continue booking meetings through both channels every single day. According to Cleanlist's 2026 cold email benchmark report, high-performing email campaigns can still achieve reply rates between 8% and 12% , though those results typically require excellent targeting, personalization, and deliverability. Phone outreach faces an equally difficult environment. GrowthList's 2026 research reports that 87% of Americans routinely ignore calls from unknown numbers , making it increasingly difficult for sales teams to reach decision makers. The data paints a clear picture: cold outreach still works, but earning attention is becoming more competitive every year. What Is Cold Calling? Unlike email, where you might wait several days for a reply, a phone call creates immediate interaction. Cold calls are basically all those calls that go out to different prospects on your lead list. As far as the latter is concerned, ALWAYS have a verified lead list that’s catered to your business requirements, or whatever product you’re selling. How does that happen? You need to start off with ICP research and document creation that’s specific to your business workflow and requirements. If you don’t know what an ICP is, or how to go on about creating one, you should read this post from Trellus.ai experts: How to Identify the Ideal B2B Prospect for Your Business Moving on, based on your cold call, if the prospect answers, you can introduce yourself, ask questions, respond to objections, and qualify the opportunity within minutes. Despite countless predictions about its decline, cold calling continues to perform well across enterprise software, professional services, commercial real estate, financial services, manufacturing, and many other industries where trust plays a major role in purchasing decisions. The biggest misunderstanding about cold calling comes from outdated stereotypes. Many people picture aggressive sales representatives interrupting strangers with long scripted pitches. Modern cold calling looks very different. The conversation feels natural because it is built around relevance, not pressure. A phone call works much better when it appears within a broader multichannel sales outreach strategy. The prospect may have already seen your LinkedIn profile, received a personalized email, or visited your website before answering the call. Several best practices continue to separate productive cold calling teams from average performers. Research every high value account before calling. Keep opening conversations concise and respectful. Speak calmly and naturally. Make every call relevant to the prospect's business. Leave professional voicemail messages when appropriate. Follow regional compliance requirements, including TCPA and Do Not Call regulations. Continue the conversation through email and LinkedIn after the call. Pros of Cold Emailing Cold email has remained one of the strongest pillars of outbound sales prospecting because it gives sales teams something every growing business wants, reach without proportional cost. That does not mean sending thousands of generic templates and hoping someone replies. Those days are disappearing quickly. Modern cold email succeeds because personalization has become easier, AI can reduce research time, and sales teams have much better visibility into campaign performance than they did a few years ago. For companies selling SaaS products, agencies, consulting services, enterprise software, financial services, or almost any B2B solution, cold email continues to generate qualified conversations every day. Here are the biggest advantages. 1. You Can Reach Thousands of Prospects Without Building a Huge Sales Team One of the biggest strengths of cold email is scale. A salesperson has only so many hours available each day. Phone calls require uninterrupted attention, while emails can be prepared, scheduled, and delivered throughout the day without someone sitting beside the keyboard. This allows a relatively small sales team to reach a very large market. With proper personalization and healthy sending practices, one SDR can comfortably manage outreach to hundreds or even thousands of qualified prospects every week. AI research tools make this even more practical because they can gather company information, identify recent hiring activity, summarize news, and suggest personalized opening lines within minutes. That does not mean every email should sound automated. The companies seeing the strongest results are the ones combining automation with thoughtful personalization. Their emails still feel like they were written for one specific recipient. This approach allows growing companies to expand their pipeline without immediately hiring large outbound teams. 2. Cold Email Is One of the Lowest Cost Lead Generation Channels Every outbound activity has a cost. Phone calls require representatives to spend time dialing, leaving voicemails, speaking with gatekeepers, handling objections, and documenting conversations. Email requires preparation too, but once campaigns are built properly, the cost per prospect becomes dramatically lower. A single sales representative can continue generating opportunities while spending much less time repeating the same introductory conversation. That efficiency has made email one of the most affordable B2B lead generation strategies available today. Many companies invest their savings into better prospect research, stronger personalization, and improved sales technology, which creates an even healthier return over time. The financial advantage becomes even more noticeable for startups and smaller businesses operating with limited sales budgets. Instead of hiring several representatives immediately, one experienced SDR supported by the right tools can generate a surprisingly healthy pipeline. 3. Prospects Can Respond When It Suits Their Schedule One reason buyers appreciate email is flexibility. Executives spend much of their day in meetings, traveling, managing teams, or solving operational problems. Answering an unexpected phone call is not always convenient. An email allows them to engage when they have a few quiet minutes available. They can read it during their commute, after finishing meetings, early in the morning, or later in the evening without feeling interrupted. This flexibility becomes even more valuable for companies selling internationally. A business based in North America may be prospecting across Europe, Asia, Australia, and the Middle East at the same time. Coordinating phone calls across every time zone becomes difficult very quickly. Email removes that obstacle. Messages can be scheduled according to each recipient's local business hours, helping outreach arrive when buyers are most likely to check their inbox. 4. Every Campaign Produces Useful Data Another major advantage of cold email is measurement. Every campaign generates information that helps sales teams improve future outreach. You can compare subject lines. You can measure reply rates. You can evaluate different calls to action. You can identify which industries respond more positively. You can discover which messaging performs best for founders, sales leaders, marketing executives, or operations teams. This continuous learning process makes email an excellent channel for refining messaging before rolling it out across larger campaigns. Small improvements across hundreds or thousands of emails often produce significant increases in cold outreach response rates over several months. 5. Sales Representatives Experience Less Emotional Burnout Outbound sales is mentally demanding. Cold calling exposes representatives to frequent rejection. Some prospects hang up immediately. Others refuse to continue the conversation. Some are polite, while others are not. Handling that level of rejection every day requires resilience. Cold email reduces much of that emotional pressure. Representatives spend more time researching accounts, improving personalization, analyzing campaign performance, and refining messaging than recovering from constant rejection. That usually creates a healthier working rhythm. Salespeople can concentrate on writing stronger emails and developing better outreach strategies rather than worrying about every unsuccessful interaction. This often improves consistency over the long term, which is one of the biggest drivers of successful outbound prospecting. Cons of Cold Emailing Cold email remains incredibly effective, but it also comes with limitations. Many of the disadvantages are not caused by email itself. They come from poor data quality, weak messaging, poor deliverability practices, or unrealistic expectations. Understanding these weaknesses allows sales teams to avoid common mistakes before they damage campaign performance. 1. Your Email Competes With Hundreds of Others Every Day Modern buyers receive an overwhelming number of emails. Internal communication, customer requests, newsletters, marketing campaigns, invoices, calendar invitations, and vendor outreach all compete for attention. Your cold email enters that crowded environment with one major disadvantage. The recipient has never heard of you. That means every sentence must earn attention immediately. Long introductions, generic value propositions, and obvious templates rarely survive beyond the first few seconds. Many emails disappear without being opened. Others are skimmed briefly before being archived. Some are deleted almost instantly. That is why relevance has become one of the strongest drivers of cold outreach response rates . Sales representatives who demonstrate genuine research consistently outperform those relying on generic messaging. 2. Deliverability Can Destroy Even Great Campaigns Writing an excellent email means very little if nobody receives it. Deliverability has become one of the biggest concerns in outbound sales. Mailbox providers continue strengthening spam detection. Google, Microsoft, and other providers evaluate domain reputation, authentication settings, complaint rates, bounce rates, engagement history, and sending behavior before deciding where your email appears. A poorly managed campaign can quickly damage domain reputation. Recovery often takes weeks or months. Healthy outbound programs invest considerable time in maintaining proper infrastructure. That includes authenticated domains, verified prospect lists, inbox warm up, gradual volume increases, and careful monitoring of campaign health. Many businesses focus heavily on copywriting while overlooking these technical foundations. Unfortunately, outstanding copy cannot compensate for poor inbox placement. Pros of Cold Calling Cold calling has survived every prediction about its disappearance for one simple reason. It continues to create conversations that turn into revenue. Technology has changed dramatically over the last decade. AI can research accounts, write personalized emails, summarize company news, and even recommend the best prospects to contact. None of those advancements have changed one basic fact. Business is still built on conversations. A live discussion allows you to understand the buyer's priorities, answer questions, handle objections, and establish credibility far faster than an email thread. That is why cold calling continues to play an important role in outbound sales prospecting , especially for companies selling complex services, enterprise software, consulting, agencies, financial services, manufacturing, and other high value B2B solutions. Here are the biggest reasons experienced sales teams continue investing in cold calling. 1. You Can Qualify Prospects Within Minutes One of the biggest advantages of cold calling is speed. Email often requires several touchpoints before you know if someone is interested. A prospect might open your message today, reply three days later, request information next week, and finally agree to a meeting after another follow up. A phone conversation compresses that entire process. If the right person answers, you can quickly understand their situation, ask thoughtful questions, identify business priorities, and determine if there is genuine potential for a future opportunity. You also gain information that email rarely provides. How urgent is the problem? Who makes the buying decision? Are they already evaluating other vendors? What solution are they currently using? Is there a budget available? These answers help sales representatives prioritize the strongest opportunities while removing poor fit accounts from the pipeline much earlier. That makes cold calling one of the fastest qualification tools available in modern sales. 2. A Phone Conversation Commands More Attention Emails compete with hundreds of other messages every day. Phone calls create a different experience. When someone answers their phone, they are giving you their full attention, even if only for thirty seconds. Those few seconds matter more than you probably think. A calm introduction, a relevant observation, and a thoughtful question can quickly determine if the conversation deserves another few minutes. Even when the prospect cannot speak immediately, your company name becomes familiar. The next email they receive from you no longer comes from a complete stranger. The next LinkedIn connection request feels more recognizable. Every touchpoint begins reinforcing the previous one. This is one of the reasons multichannel sales outreach performs better than relying on only one communication channel. Recognition builds trust long before a meeting is scheduled. 3. Trust Develops Much Faster Through Voice Buying decisions involve people. People evaluate confidence, professionalism, sincerity, and credibility during conversation. Voice communicates those qualities much better than written text. A calm, respectful conversation allows prospects to hear your personality, ask questions naturally, and judge your expertise in real time. This becomes especially valuable in industries where purchases involve significant financial investment or operational risk. Enterprise software. Financial services. Healthcare. Professional consulting. Commercial real estate. Managed IT services. Buyers in these industries rarely make purchasing decisions based solely on email exchanges. 4. Objections Can Be Handled Immediately Every buyer has concerns. Phone calls create immediate dialogue. If a prospect says they are already working with another provider, you can ask what they like about that relationship. If they mention budget limitations, you can understand their purchasing process. If timing is the concern, you can identify when a future conversation would make more sense. This natural exchange prevents misunderstandings from growing into lost opportunities. Also Read: How to Handle Sales Objections: Best Proven Techniques for 2026 It also helps sales representatives understand which objections appear repeatedly across different industries. That information improves future messaging across the entire sales organization. 5. You Can Reach Decision Makers More Directly Senior executives receive enormous volumes of email every day. Many messages never receive a reply. Some are delegated; others remain unread for weeks. A carefully timed phone call often provides a faster path to the decision maker. Founders, owners, managing directors, and executives still answer their phones, especially when caller identification appears local or familiar. That does not mean every executive welcomes cold calls. Far from it. It simply means that a respectful, relevant conversation still has a place in executive outreach. When supported with research and good timing, cold calling often creates access that email alone struggles to achieve. For organizations selling premium services or enterprise solutions, that access can make an enormous difference. Cons of Cold Calling Cold calling continues to produce excellent results, but no outbound channel is perfect. It demands preparation, resilience, patience, and discipline. Many organizations underestimate these requirements, which explains why some teams abandon cold calling long before they begin seeing meaningful results. Understanding these limitations allows businesses to decide where cold calling fits within their broader outreach strategy. 1. Connecting With the Right Person Takes Time One of the biggest frustrations in cold calling is simply reaching someone. Many calls end in voicemail. Others are answered by gatekeepers, and they normally keep you on the hook by saying that either they’ll pass your message on to the concerned person, or someone will get back to you. But, it never, or rarely happens! Even highly experienced representatives spend much of their time attempting connections rather than holding conversations. That reality surprises many companies entering outbound sales for the first time. Success in cold calling comes from persistence and consistency rather than immediate results. A representative may need dozens of quality dials before speaking with someone who matches the ideal customer profile. The stronger your prospect list, the more productive every calling session becomes. 2. Frequent Rejection Can Affect Performance Occasionally, representatives encounter frustration or irritation from buyers who were interrupted during a busy moment. Handling these interactions day after day requires emotional resilience. Without strong coaching and supportive leadership, motivation can begin to decline. That is why successful outbound organizations invest heavily in regular coaching sessions, call reviews, role playing, and skill development. Representatives who receive constructive feedback usually recover much faster after unsuccessful conversations. Over time, they become more confident, more adaptable, and significantly more effective. 3. Cold Calling Requires Strong Communication Skills Sending a good email demands careful writing. Holding a productive phone conversation requires several skills working together at the same time. Representatives must listen carefully. They need to ask thoughtful questions. They must think quickly when unexpected objections appear. They need confidence without sounding aggressive. They must guide conversations naturally while remaining respectful of the prospect's time. These abilities improve with practice. Companies expecting immediate success from inexperienced callers are often disappointed because effective cold calling remains a learned skill. Regular coaching, call recordings, peer feedback, and repetition make a substantial difference. Wrapping It Up As we mentioned at the beginning of this insightful post, it’s all about using either a blend of both approaches or taking either one as the first step. But customization and proper research, alongside KPIs, are the main key players here. Otherwise, you’re just going to be missing out on opportunities that could’ve been seized from the very beginning.

title: Mortgage rates today, June 18: Fed dot plot sends rates higher
summary: Mortgage rates climbed Wednesday after the Fed's updated dot plot signaled a higher-for-longer rate path. The average 30-year fixed is 6.62% today. Here's what moved rates and what buyers should know.
body_text: All rates listed in this article are daily averages based on Better Mortgage data and not personalized rates or APRs. Average rates show trends. Real rates vary by borrower. Average mortgage rates climbed sharply on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve's updated dot plot signaled that policymakers expect the federal funds rate to end 2026 at least 0.25% higher than they projected in March. The average 30-year fixed rate is 6.62% today, erasing the gains from last week's one-month lows and returning rates to mid-June levels. Rates vary depending on the source and methodology; see the table below and the note at the end of this article. For buyers and homeowners monitoring the market, here is what moved rates this week and what it means for decisions you may be facing today. Today's mortgage rates — June 18, 2026 Loan type Average rate 30-year fixed 6.62% 15-year fixed 6.16% 5/1 ARM 6.47% APR 30-year fixed refinance 6.66% 15-year fixed refinance 6.05% These are national averages — your actual rate and APR depends on your credit score, down payment, loan amount, and lender. See your custom rate ...in as little as 3 minutes — no credit impact Mortgage rates vary across sources — you may see figures ranging from 6.39% to 6.62% for the 30-year fixed today. That range reflects different methodologies: some sources report APR, which includes lender fees and results in a higher number, while others report the raw interest rate. Data from different lender pools and survey timing also contribute. The rates in the table above reflect interest rate averages based on Better Mortgage data. For a personalized rate based on your specific credit profile, loan amount, and down payment, the most accurate step is to get a rate quote directly. Why mortgage rates jumped today The move higher traces directly to Wednesday afternoon's Federal Reserve meeting, which produced two market-moving signals in quick succession. The first was the dot plot, a chart the Fed releases every other meeting showing where each policymaker expects the federal funds rate to be in the future. Wednesday's update showed that, on average, Fed members now expect the funds rate to end 2026 higher than they projected in March. Investors read this as a message that rate cuts are further away than markets had assumed. The second signal came from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference. Markets had hoped Warsh would push back against the dot plot with a more rate-friendly tone; instead, his comments gave little guidance on how the Fed is interpreting incoming economic data. When the central bank's reaction function is unclear, bond investors tend to demand a higher risk premium, and because mortgage rates are priced off mortgage-backed securities, which in turn follow Treasury yields, that uncertainty flowed directly into lender rate sheets. Some lenders repriced their offerings two or three times on Wednesday afternoon. When the dust settled, the average 30-year fixed had risen 8 basis points. (One basis point is one hundredth of a percent.) The increase returned average rates to the levels seen in early June, before last week's brief improvement tied to progress in U.S.-Iran ceasefire talks. What the rate environment means for buyers right now Rates are elevated, but the direction of movement this week matters as much as the level. The brief dip to one-month lows last week followed news that the U.S. and Iran had reached an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. That improvement has now been reversed, reinforcing a pattern that has characterized this market for months: any rate relief tied to geopolitical developments proves short-lived when the underlying inflation and Fed-policy picture remains unresolved. Industry forecasters broadly expect 30-year rates to remain above 6% for the rest of 2026. A meaningful move lower would require either a sustained decline in inflation data or a clear signal from the Fed that rate cuts are back on the table — neither of which is imminent based on Wednesday's communication. That said, rates at 6.62% are not historically extreme. The structural reality for most buyers is that waiting for a meaningful drop risks being sidelined indefinitely in a market where home prices in many areas continue to hold. On rate lock timing: lock when you have a rate you can afford, not when you're trying to time the bottom. Many lenders offer float-down options that allow you to lock a rate and then move to a lower rate should it drop materially before closing. That optionality is worth asking about, but it's not a reason to delay locking if you're close to closing. How to get the lowest rate available to you The rates in the table above are averages. What you're actually offered depends on your individual profile, and there are meaningful levers in your control. Credit score Lenders tier their pricing by credit score. Borrowers with scores of 740 or higher typically receive rates 0.25%–0.50% below the published average. If your score is below 680, spending a few months improving it before applying can have a larger impact on your rate than waiting for market rates to drop. Learn about the minimum credit score needed for a mortgage and what drives your pricing tier. Down payment Putting down 20% eliminates private mortgage insurance (PMI) and typically earns you a better rate. If 20% isn't feasible, conventional loans allow as little as 3% down, and FHA loans allow 3.5% with a 580+ credit score. Understand how much down payment you actually need before assuming 20% is the threshold you have to meet. Loan type The 15-year fixed at 6.16% carries a lower rate than the 30-year at 6.62% — a 46-basis-point difference. The tradeoff is a higher monthly payment, because you're repaying the same principal in half the time. A 5/1 ARM offers a lower initial rate but adjusts annually after the five-year fixed period. Comparing FHA vs. conventional loan options can also affect both your rate and total cost depending on your down payment and credit profile. Shopping lenders Rates differ meaningfully from lender to lender for the same borrower profile. Getting quotes from more than one lender before committing is one of the most direct ways to reduce your rate. With Better, you can get pre-approved online in as little as three minutes without affecting your credit score — giving you a real rate to compare against other offers. Fed Chair Warsh's press conference added uncertainty by providing little guidance on the Fed's reaction to incoming data. Bond investors responded by demanding higher yields, and mortgage rates followed. Is 6.62% a good mortgage rate in June 2026? 6.62% is above the 2026 year-to-date average of roughly 6.25% but below the peaks seen earlier in the year. Whether it's "good" depends on your credit profile and the alternatives available to you. Borrowers with strong credit and larger down payments can often beat the average. The more relevant question is whether the rate fits your budget, and whether waiting is realistic given current forecasts. What is the Fed dot plot and why does it affect my mortgage rate? The dot plot is a chart showing where each Federal Reserve policymaker individually expects the federal funds rate to be in the future. It gets released every other Fed meeting. When the dot plot shifts upward — suggesting fewer or later rate cuts — bond investors reprice Treasuries and mortgage-backed securities higher, which flows into the mortgage rates lenders offer. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates directly, but its signaling moves the bond market that does. Should I lock my mortgage rate now or wait? Rate timing is genuinely uncertain. The standard guidance is to lock when you have a rate you can afford, rather than speculating on where rates are headed. If you're close to closing, the risk of waiting typically outweighs the potential benefit. Ask your lender about float-down options, which allow you to lock now and potentially move to a lower rate if rates fall materially before closing. What's the difference between a mortgage interest rate and APR? The interest rate is the cost of borrowing the principal, expressed as a percentage. APR (annual percentage rate) includes the interest rate plus other loan costs such as origination fees, mortgage insurance, and discount points. APR is always higher than or equal to the interest rate. Different sources use different measures, which is why you may see rates ranging from 6.39% to 6.62% for the 30-year fixed today. How much does a 0.25% rate increase affect my monthly payment? On a $400,000 loan, a 0.25 percentage point increase in your rate adds roughly $65–$70 per month to your principal and interest payment, or about $800 per year. Use a mortgage calculator to estimate the impact at your specific loan amount and down payment. Are mortgage rates expected to go down in 2026? Industry forecasters broadly expect rates to remain above 6% for the rest of 2026, with modest downward drift possible if inflation data cooperates. A material drop would require a significant shift in both the inflation picture and Fed policy, conditions not currently in view. Planning your purchase around today's rates, rather than waiting for rates that may not materialize, is the approach most professionals recommend. Do VA or FHA loans offer lower rates than conventional mortgages? VA loans typically carry rates slightly below conventional loans for eligible borrowers — veterans, active-duty service members, and eligible surviving spouses — with no down payment requirement and no monthly mortgage insurance. FHA loans also often offer competitive rates for borrowers with lower credit scores. Comparing VA loan vs. conventional and FHA vs. conventional options can help you identify the most cost-effective path. The bottom line The 30-year fixed mortgage rate is 6.62% today, pushed higher by the Federal Reserve's hawkish dot plot and a press conference that gave markets little comfort about the path ahead. The brief improvement from last week has been fully reversed. For buyers in the market, the practical reality is that rates above 6% are likely here through at least the end of the year — and the levers most in your control are your credit score, down payment, and choice of loan and lender. summary: Netflix heard the fans loud and clear! Here the Whole Time, an adaptation of Vitor Martins's bestseller starring Miguel Lallo and Diego Lira, will be available for streaming worldwide on August 19.
body_text: São Paulo, July 14, 2026 — Netflix heard the fans loud and clear! Here the Whole Time , an adaptation of Vitor Martins's bestseller starring Miguel Lallo and Diego Lira, will be available for streaming worldwide on August 19 . To celebrate the news, Netflix brought the stars of the movie to London for a get-together with Kit Connor and Joe Locke, stars of the feature Heartstopper Forever , which premieres on July 17 and marks the end of the hit franchise inspired by Alice Oseman's graphic novel. (Photo Credit: Netflix) Based on books that have captivated readers around the world, Here the Whole Time – which fans lovingly call the “ Brazilian Heartstopper” — and the UK show share themes such as youth, LGBTQIA+ identity, belonging and the discoveries of first love. The actors' meeting highlighted the connection between the stories and celebrated the new Netflix releases. After moving audiences in theaters, Here the Whole Time will be available to watch, rewatch and binge on Netflix whenever you want, as many times as you like, starting August 19. About Here the Whole Time Synopsis: Felipe (Miguel Lallo), a sensitive teenager with a passion for pop culture, just wants to survive the summer break — staying away from the school bullies, binge-watching his favorite shows and forgetting about the outside world. But his plans go awry when his self-assured neighbor Caio (Diego Lira), the popular guy at school and his old crush, moves in under the same roof for two weeks. About Heartstopper Forever Synopsis: Nick (Kit Connor) and Charlie (Joe Locke) are inseparable, but with Nick about to leave for university and Charlie discovering a new independence at school, the reality of a long-distance relationship starts to weigh on them. Doubts begin to set in, and their relationship faces its biggest challenge yet. Meanwhile, the couple's friends are also navigating the ups and downs of love and friendship, facing the pains and joys of growing up and forging their own paths. Can first love really last forever? About Conspiração Conspiração is one of Brazil’s leading independent production companies, founded by filmmakers and built around Brazilian artistic creation. With 10 International Emmy nominations – the most for any independent production company in Latin America – Conspiração co-produced I'm Still Here , winner of the Academy Award® for Best International Feature Film and the Golden Globe® for Best Actress – Drama. The production company is also behind five of the biggest box office hits in Brazilian cinema. Conspiração's projects have premiered at major international festivals, including Cannes, Berlin, Sundance, Venice, and Toronto. With more than 50 feature films, 30 series, and 45 documentaries produced, totaling more than 30 million tickets sold at the box office and over 300 awards, the company combines a strong artistic vision with projects that reach both Brazilian audiences and the international market, rooted in the strength of Brazilian storytelling. About Manequim Filmes Manequim Filmes, Vitrine group's commercial distribution label, was created to bring the best of Brazilian cinema to wider audiences. In just three years, Manequim has already established itself in the audiovisual market with Brazil’s highest-grossing national release of 2023: Our Dream – The Story of Claudinho and Buchecha . In 2026, it released The King of the Internet , the story of Brazilian hacker Daniel Nascimento and Here the Whole Time , based on the bestseller by Vítor Martins. The Vitrine Filmes Group has distributed more than 300 films over the course of more than 15 years. Its biggest successes include The Secret Agent, Bacurau , Invisible Life and The Way He Looks . Its documentary releases include Pictures of Ghosts , Divine Divas , The Trial and Secret Friend . About Netflix Netflix is one of the world’s leading entertainment services offering TV series, films, games and live programming across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time. Press Kit Agência Ágora | netflix@agora.site

title: Startup PR vs LinkedIn for Founders: Where Credibility Actually Compounds
summary: Startup PR can create useful credibility spikes, but LinkedIn gives founders the repeatable surface where trust compounds before buyers, investors, and candidates are ready to act.
body_text: Startup PR vs LinkedIn for Founders: Where Credibility Actually Compounds Startup PR has a clean story. A founder gets quoted in a respected publication. The company announces a raise. A product launch gets covered. The logo goes on the website. Investors notice. Candidates see momentum. Buyers get a third-party signal that the company is real. That signal matters. But most founders overestimate what PR can do by itself. Press can create a spike of attention. It can validate a moment. It can make a company easier to trust when someone is already looking. What it usually cannot do is build a repeated relationship with the market every week. That is where LinkedIn is different. LinkedIn is not a replacement for startup PR. It is the place where the founder turns market judgment into repeated visibility. PR says someone noticed you. LinkedIn shows why the market should keep paying attention. This guide breaks down startup PR vs LinkedIn for founders: what each channel is good at, where each one fails, when to invest in PR, when to prioritize founder-led LinkedIn, and how to make the two work together without turning the founder into a full-time content operator. ‍ What Startup PR Actually Does Startup PR is public relations for startups: media relationships, announcements, founder commentary, thought leadership placements, podcast appearances, analyst mentions, awards, and other third-party visibility. The strongest PR creates borrowed credibility. A buyer may not know the company, but they know the publication. An investor may not have met the founder, but they see market validation. A candidate may not understand the category, but they see momentum from outside the company's own website. That is useful because early and growth-stage companies have a trust deficit. The product may be strong, but the market has not had enough time to decide whether the company matters. PR can shorten that distance. For founders, PR is especially useful around moments: funding announcements, major customer wins, category shifts, original data, executive hires, product launches, partnerships, and strong points of view on a timely market story. The mistake is treating PR like a permanent demand engine. A press hit can create attention. It does not automatically create a content system, a sales narrative, or a founder voice the market learns to recognize. ‍ Why Founders Overestimate PR Founders overestimate PR because press feels concrete. There is a headline. There is a link. There is a logo. There may be a traffic spike, a few investor texts, and a burst of employee excitement. Compared with the slow compounding of founder-led content, PR feels like a win you can point to. But the shelf life is short. Most articles get one wave of distribution. The audience sees the story, reacts if it matters, and moves on. Unless the company has a way to keep the conversation alive, the press hit becomes a credibility artifact instead of a growth channel. PR also depends on external timing. A founder can have a strong story and still lose the cycle to bigger news. A reporter can be interested and still never publish. A launch can be meaningful to the company but not newsworthy to the market. That does not make PR bad. It makes PR episodic. Founders get into trouble when they expect an episodic channel to do a compounding channel's job. PR can validate a moment. LinkedIn can turn that moment into repeated market education. ‍ What LinkedIn Does That PR Cannot LinkedIn gives founders control over the cadence. A founder does not need a reporter to approve a post about a customer pattern, a category belief, a hiring lesson, a sales objection, or a product decision. They can publish directly to the market and see what happens. That speed matters because B2B trust is built through repetition. Buyers rarely change their mind because of one article. Investors rarely build conviction from one quote. Candidates rarely decide a founder is worth following from one announcement. They need repeated exposure to how the founder thinks. LinkedIn makes that possible. A founder can explain the problem before the buyer is ready to buy. They can make the category feel urgent before the sales team reaches out. They can show judgment before a fundraising process starts. They can answer objections in public before those objections show up on calls. This is the same reason founder-led marketing works. The founder becomes the clearest carrier of the company's market belief, because the founder is closest to the customer, product, category, and risk. PR can amplify credibility. LinkedIn can manufacture familiarity. ‍ Startup PR vs LinkedIn: The Real Difference The real difference is not earned media versus social media. The real difference is borrowed trust versus repeated trust. Startup PR borrows trust from a publication, podcast, analyst, community, or third-party voice. That borrowed trust is valuable when the audience respects the source. It can help a young company look more legitimate faster. LinkedIn builds repeated trust through the founder's own voice. The market sees the founder make claims, explain tradeoffs, respond to comments, share customer patterns, and take a position over time. The trust is not borrowed. It is earned in public. Both matter, but they solve different problems. Use PR when the company has a moment the market should notice. Use LinkedIn when the founder has a point of view the market should remember. Use PR to make a milestone more credible. Use LinkedIn to explain why the milestone matters. Use PR when a third-party source can validate the company. Use LinkedIn when the founder needs to teach the market how to think about the problem. The best B2B founders do not choose one forever. They know which job they are hiring each channel to do. ‍ When Startup PR Wins Startup PR wins when third-party validation matters more than direct explanation. Funding is the obvious example. A raise is not just capital. It is a market signal. A good funding announcement can support investor relations, recruiting, customer confidence, and partner interest. LinkedIn can distribute the story, but the outside coverage gives it weight. PR also wins when the company has original data. If a startup can show a market shift with credible numbers, a reporter or industry publication can help the insight travel beyond the founder's immediate network. PR is useful for category moments. When regulation changes, a new platform launches, a market breaks, or a well-known company creates a debate, a founder with a sharp take can become part of the public conversation. PR helps with legitimacy in conservative markets. Enterprise buyers, public-sector buyers, financial services buyers, and risk-sensitive categories often care about external proof. A strong press footprint can reduce the feeling that the company is too unknown. PR can also help with executive recruiting. Senior candidates want to know whether the company has momentum. Coverage gives them something to inspect beyond the careers page. In all of those cases, PR is doing the job it should do: creating external validation around a real moment. ‍ When LinkedIn Wins LinkedIn wins when the market needs repetition, education, and founder trust. If buyers do not fully understand the problem yet, LinkedIn is stronger than PR. The founder can explain the pain from different angles every week. They can name the pattern buyers feel but have not articulated. They can make the category more urgent through repeated examples. If the company sells into a long B2B sales cycle, LinkedIn is stronger. Buyers may not be ready today, but they can still become familiar with the founder's thinking long before procurement starts. If the founder's judgment is part of the sale, LinkedIn is stronger. This is common in founder-led companies, technical products, new categories, and high-trust services. Buyers want to know whether the founder actually understands the market. If fundraising visibility matters, LinkedIn is stronger between announcements. PR can support the raise when the moment arrives. LinkedIn builds the track record investors quietly watch before the meeting. That connects directly to what investors look for in a founder's LinkedIn . If sales needs warmer context, LinkedIn is stronger. A founder post can become an outbound opener, a follow-up asset, an objection handler, or a reason for a buyer to accept a connection. That is why founder-led sales on LinkedIn is not just posting. It is sales context created before the pitch. LinkedIn wins when the work is not one big announcement. It wins when the market needs to hear the same founder make the same sharp point in enough ways that it finally sticks. ‍ The Best Workflow Uses Both The strongest workflow is not PR or LinkedIn. It is PR plus founder-led distribution. Before a PR moment, the founder should use LinkedIn to prepare the market. If a funding announcement is coming, publish the category thesis before the round is public. If a product launch is coming, explain the customer problem and the old way that is breaking. If original data is coming, test the underlying narrative in posts first. During the PR moment, LinkedIn should translate the headline into founder thinking. Do not just repost the article with a generic caption. Explain what the milestone reveals, why the company made the bet, what customer pattern led to it, and what the market should understand next. After the PR moment, LinkedIn should keep the story alive. Break the coverage into smaller ideas. Turn the founder quote into a post. Turn the customer problem into a series. Turn the data into sales enablement. Turn the announcement into recruiting context. This is how PR stops being a one-day spike and becomes part of a larger content system. A single press hit can support weeks of founder-led content if the team knows how to extract the underlying point of view. ‍ How to Decide Where to Invest First Founders should invest first in the channel that matches the current constraint. If the company lacks credibility around a major milestone, PR may be the right move. A strong announcement can make the market take the company more seriously. If the company lacks a clear narrative, LinkedIn should come first. PR cannot fix a weak point of view. If the founder cannot explain what the market gets wrong, why the problem matters, and why the company is credible, press will only expose the lack of clarity. If the company needs pipeline, LinkedIn usually comes first. PR can create awareness, but founder-led LinkedIn is better at building repeated familiarity with buyers and giving sales usable context. If the company needs investor awareness months before a raise, LinkedIn comes first. PR is useful when there is news. LinkedIn is useful before there is news. If the company has original data or a genuinely timely market angle, PR may come first. But the LinkedIn plan should be ready before the story goes live. The practical rule is simple: PR works better when the founder already has a point of view. LinkedIn is how that point of view gets built, tested, and sharpened. ‍ What to Measure Do not measure PR and LinkedIn with the same scoreboard. For PR, track the quality of the placement, relevance of the audience, referral traffic, branded search lift, investor or customer replies, candidate mentions, sales usage, and whether the story created a credibility asset the team can reuse. For LinkedIn, track profile views, follower quality, comments from the right people, DMs, connection requests, sales-call mentions, target-account engagement, investor familiarity, and topic patterns that create pipeline signal. The shared question is whether the channel moved the right people closer. That is the same lens behind LinkedIn ROI for founders . The value is not always visible in a clean attribution report. Sometimes it shows up as a warmer reply, a faster investor meeting, a candidate who already understands the mission, or a buyer who says they have been following the founder for months. PR and LinkedIn both create trust. The mistake is pretending trust always converts on the same day it is created. ‍ Common Mistakes Founders Make The first mistake is using PR before the narrative is ready. If the story is vague, press will not make it sharper. The second mistake is treating a press hit as the finish line. The coverage is the start of distribution, not the end. The third mistake is reposting articles without founder commentary. A link alone does not teach the market anything. The founder has to explain why the story matters. The fourth mistake is chasing publications the buyer does not read. A smaller industry placement can be more useful than a broad startup mention if the right operators see it. The fifth mistake is outsourcing the founder's point of view. A PR team can pitch. A content team can edit. But the market needs the founder's real judgment, not a sanitized quote that sounds like every other startup announcement. The sixth mistake is separating PR, sales, and LinkedIn. If sales does not know which story is live, they cannot use it. If LinkedIn does not extend the story, it fades. If PR does not understand the founder's public narrative, it pitches disconnected moments. The channels should reinforce one another. ‍ How Rethoric Thinks About PR and LinkedIn Rethoric's view is that PR is strongest when it has founder-led content around it. The founder should not show up only when there is an announcement. By then, the market has no context. The best founders build the context first. They publish the category thesis, customer patterns, hard lessons, product beliefs, and market frustrations before the press cycle needs them. Then, when PR lands, the audience already has a reason to care. That requires a system. Founders need a way to capture raw thinking, turn it into sharp posts, approve without slowing down, schedule consistently, engage with the right people, tag content by theme, and measure which ideas create business signal. That is what keeps founder-led LinkedIn from becoming random posting. It also makes PR more useful, because every external mention has a stronger narrative to plug into. PR gives the market proof that something happened. LinkedIn helps the founder explain what it means. ‍ The Bottom Line on Startup PR vs LinkedIn Startup PR and LinkedIn are not enemies. They are different trust tools. PR creates credibility spikes around moments that deserve outside validation. LinkedIn creates repeated familiarity with the founder's judgment before buyers, investors, candidates, and partners are ready to act. If you only do PR, the market may notice you and forget why it should care. If you only do LinkedIn, you may build familiarity but miss moments where third-party validation would strengthen the story. The strongest founders use LinkedIn to build the point of view, PR to validate important moments, and founder-led content to keep the story alive after the headline fades. If you want founder-led LinkedIn content with strategy, capture, approvals, scheduling, engagement, tagging, mobile review, and analytics, see how Rethoric works with founders .

title: Virtual Event Production: 7-Step Guide, Tools & Strategies
summary: Avoid low participation and disengaged audiences. This guide covers key steps, tools & common pitfalls for high-quality virtual event production.
body_text: Without the right tools and strategy, your virtual event could yield high registration numbers but low participation, flat presentations that don’t hold attention, and missed follow-up opportunities. To avoid wasted investment and results that reflect poorly on your decision-making, your approach needs to address not only professional production quality but also a streamlined end-to-end workflow that considers everything from setup to post-event follow-up. This guide walks you through the key steps of virtual event production, from defining goals and choosing the right platform to audience engagement and post-event follow-up. You’ll also learn common mistakes to avoid and how to optimize your event for maximum ROI. Whether you’re focused on lead generation, customer education, or brand positioning, this guide will help you plan, execute, and refine a high-performing virtual event. What is virtual event production? Components, benefits & objectives Virtual event production is the process of planning, executing, and managing an event hosted online using digital tools and technology. It requires a combination of: Broadcast-quality content Audience engagement strategies Engagement and performance analytics When these core elements work together effectively, you create a professional, interactive experience that keeps attendees engaged, whether your event is live or on-demand. Key benefits of virtual event production Virtual events enable you to create engaging, data-driven webinars and digital experiences that support pipeline growth, customer education, and brand positioning. Here’s how they can help you achieve these goals: Scalable processes: Automation and interactive tools streamline event management, allowing you to engage more attendees without added workload. Continued value: Recorded sessions, interactive discussions, and on-demand access ensure your key messaging resonates long after the event ends. Built-in data and analytics: Real-time insights into audience behavior, session performance, and engagement trends allow for continual optimization. Audience targeting: With flexible formatting and integrated marketing tools, you can tailor content for specific industries, job roles, or stages in the buyer journey. Primary goals and objectives A strong virtual event strategy is outcome-driven, with clear objectives that align with business and marketing priorities. Audience engagement: Keeping attendees involved through interactive features like Q&As, polls, and networking sessions creates a more memorable, positive experience. Lead generation: Virtual events provide multiple touchpoints for capturing qualified leads and guiding them through the sales funnel with targeted content. Brand positioning: By delivering valuable insights and high-quality content, you can establish your brand as an authority on relevant topics and solutions. Post-event nurturing: Recorded sessions, personalized follow-ups, and attendee insights help sustain relationships and move attendees further along the customer journey. 💡 Pro tip: Use Demio AI to automate Q&As and chat moderation so you can make personalized follow-ups based on what your audience really care about. This will give on-demand attendees a fully engaging experience and help you continually capture leads from your events. 7-Step guide to virtual event production This guide breaks down the key stages of virtual event production, from setting goals and choosing a platform to audience engagement and post-event follow-up. 1. Define your event goals and ICP Your event’s goals and audience determine key success metrics like registrant-to-attendee conversion, engagement rate, and post-event actions. These decisions shape content structure, speaker selection, and audience interaction, directly impacting ROI. Set a clear objective: Define whether your event is for lead generation, customer education, brand awareness, or networking to shape your content and structure. Narrow down your ideal audience: Identify job roles, industries, experience levels, and pain points to define your ideal audience. Use Reach for audience acquisition: Reach by Banzai helps you attract high-quality attendees that fit your ICP, so the right people show up and participate. Align content with ICP priorities: For executives, focus on high-level insights; for practitioners, include tactical and hands-on content. Use Reach to identify leads, manage your pipeline, and deploy multi-channel outbound campaigns. 2. Choose the right virtual event platform Your virtual event platform determines how easily attendees can register, join, and engage, impacting metrics like attendance rate, session duration, and post-event interactions. Choosing a unified virtual event platform that integrates audience acquisition, hosting, and post-event analytics simplifies execution and maximizes your ROI. Here’s what to prioritize: Ease of use: A seamless registration process and intuitive interface reduce drop-off rates and create a smooth hosting experience. Engagement features: Choose a platform with Q&A, polls, chat, audience reactions, and slide sharing for both live and on-demand webinars. Built-in analytics: Track attendance, session duration, and engagement metrics to measure success and refine future events. Banzai’s full-stack solution: Demio powers virtual event production with automated registration, engagement tools, and post-event analytics, Reach drives audience acquisition, and Boost amplifies event promotion—all within the Banzai ecosystem. Banzai’s family of webinar tools also includes Openreel for branded video creation and management and Vidello’s video marketing suite—so you can seamlessly create, promote, host, and analyze events with a fully integrated, end-to-end event production solution. Demio’s engagement features, automated processes, and AI solutions make virtual event production simple to execute and highly effective. 3. Plan and structure your event content A well-structured event keeps attendees engaged and ensures your key messages are delivered effectively. Thoughtful planning helps maintain momentum, balance speaker contributions, and encourage audience interaction. Here’s how to develop and structure your content: Outline the attendee journey : Define the flow from registration to post-event follow-up, ensuring each segment reinforces your core message and encourages participation. Break sessions into digestible segments: Use a mix of keynotes, panels, breakout sessions, and interactive discussions to maintain engagement while keeping messaging clear and consistent. Incorporate engagement touchpoints: Plan how to integrate Q&As, polls, and interactive chat at key moments to keep attendees actively involved. Match the format to the event type: Webinars, panel discussions, workshops, and product demos each require different content structures—use slide sharing, polls, and speaker prompts to reinforce key takeaways and drive your desired actions. 4. Set up technical requirements and production tools A strong virtual event setup goes beyond choosing the right platform—it’s about optimizing and automating every step to ensure a high-quality attendee experience and reduce manual work for your team. Using natively integrated solutions lets you streamline workflows from registration to follow-up, keeping everything connected without switching between systems. Configure integrations for seamless data flow: Connect your CRM, marketing automation, and analytics tools to sync attendee engagement, track conversions, and automate follow-ups. Automate event setup and attendee experience: Use pre-set event templates, branded registration pages, and automated reminders to minimize admin tasks and ensure a consistent experience. Optimize branding and messaging across touchpoints: Customize your registration pages, emails, and in-session branding so every interaction reinforces your brand. Simplify speaker and attendee onboarding: Provide a pre-event checklist, guided platform walkthroughs, and automated setup instructions to make participation easy for everyone. 5. Rehearse and prepare speakers Even experienced speakers need preparation to deliver their message clearly and stay within time limits. A well-run rehearsal helps you avoid awkward pauses and manage unforeseen circumstances. Hold a full tech run-through: Run a full tech check to confirm audio, video, slides, and screen-sharing are set up for a professional, polished experience. Set expectations for pacing and timing: Clarify the ideal speaking time per segment and build in transitions to keep energy high. Coach speakers on engagement strategies: Encourage them to acknowledge chat responses, refer to audience questions, and maintain a conversational tone. Have a backup plan : Have a moderator ready to step in if you have a no-show. 6. Engage your audience with interactive elements Virtual events need active participation to hold attention—otherwise, attendees passively tune out or drop off. Plan interactive moments to keep them engaged. Use polls and Q&A strategically: Schedule these at key points to break up long presentations and involve the audience. Leverage chat and reactions: Encourage real-time discussions and allow attendees to react to key moments. Offer networking opportunities: Chat threads and structured discussions help attendees connect. Incorporate gamification: Leaderboards, giveaways, and interactive challenges add excitement and keep people engaged. 7. Analyze event performance and follow up Review attendee data to identify high-intent leads, refine content for future events, and tailor follow-ups based on engagement levels. Review key event metrics: Look at attendance rates, engagement levels, and Q&A participation to evaluate performance. Gather attendee feedback: Use post-event surveys to identify what worked and what could improve. Repurpose content for continued reach: Turn key insights into blog posts, short video clips, or follow-up emails to extend the event’s impact. Send personalized follow-ups: Nurture attendees with targeted next steps, whether it’s an on-demand replay, exclusive resources, or a demo request. Mistakes to avoid in virtual event production Even experienced event organizers run into avoidable mistakes that hurt engagement and retention. Here are some real-world pitfalls and how to avoid them: Not setting up a backup engagement plan: If audience interaction is low, you need a way to pull them back in. Have pre-planned discussion prompts or a moderator ready to call on attendees directly in chat or Q&A. Underestimating pre-event marketing: Just sending an invite isn’t enough. Use multi-touch promotion—email sequences, LinkedIn posts, and targeted ads—to increase event attendance. Overcomplicating registration: If sign-up requires too many steps, drop-off increases. Simplify registration with auto-fill forms, calendar invites, and a one-click login option for attendees. Ignoring audience fatigue: Long sessions kill engagement. Break content into shorter, high-energy segments and use interactive elements every 10-15 minutes to hold attention. Not repurposing content post-event: A virtual event isn’t just a one-time experience. Clip high-value moments into short video snippets (which is super-easy with OpenReel’s video creation tools ), turn key takeaways into blog posts, and use on-demand access to extend reach. Avoiding these mistakes will increase attendance, keep audiences engaged, and extend the value of your event beyond the live session. Virtual event production: Key strategies to drive ROI A well-executed virtual event goes beyond simply hosting a webinar—it requires strategic planning, audience engagement, and post-event optimization. By setting clear goals, choosing the right platform, and structuring your content for interaction, you can maximize attendance and participation. Avoid common mistakes like focusing too much on registrations over engagement, underestimating pre-event marketing, or ignoring post-event follow-ups. Instead, leverage automation, audience insights, and interactive tools to keep attendees engaged and drive ROI. Whether you’re running a lead generation event, a customer education session, or a thought leadership panel, using a unified platform like Banzai brings together multiple webinar and marketing solutions that simplify execution and reduce your manual workload. With the right approach, your virtual event can be a valuable, high-converting experience for both your attendees and business.

title: XOMA Royalty Announces Closing of Its Acquisition by Ligand
summary: XOMA Royalty has built a significant portfolio of products that are licensed to and being developed by other biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies.  The Company’s portfolio of partner-funded programs spans multiple stages of the…
body_text: Press Releases XOMA Royalty Announces Closing of Its Acquisition by Ligand Download as PDF July 14, 2026 9:00am EDT EMERYVILLE, Calif., July 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XOMA Royalty Corporation today announced that Ligand Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (Nasdaq: LGND) has completed its previously announced acquisition of XOMA Royalty. Pursuant to the terms of the transaction announced on April 27, 2026, Ligand acquired all of the outstanding shares of XOMA Royalty common stock. XOMA Royalty stockholders received $39.00 in cash per share of XOMA Royalty common stock owned. XOMA Royalty stockholders and equity award holders also received one non-transferable Contingent Value Right (“CVR”) per share entitling the holder to receive a portion of 75% of the net proceeds that may result from certain pending litigation at XOMA Royalty. As a result of the transaction completion, XOMA Royalty’s common stock no longer trades on the Nasdaq stock exchange. Leerink Partners served as lead financial advisor, H.C.
